outcome: Prevalence of delayed initiation of breastfeeding
cohort: 404 mother-infant pairs at Mbale regional referral hospital (MRRH) in Eastern Uganda
finding: The rate of delayed initiation of breastfeeding was high and associated with several factors, including caesarean section, limited antenatal care, labor difficulties, and infant health issues at birth.
mod_finding: Caesarean section was identified as a risk factor for delayed initiation of breastfeeding (AOR = 2.07; 95%CI: 1.3-3.19).
